# Parley

> Local AI inference mesh for teams. One binary turns your machines into a shared on-premise LLM cluster.

Parley pools Apple Silicon Macs, NVIDIA workstations, and spare hardware into a single inference mesh. Models loaded on any node are usable from every node. Peer-to-peer model transfer means one download serves the whole team. Zero config, zero cloud, zero data leaks.

## Key facts

- Single binary for macOS, Linux, and Windows
- Ships its own Rust inference engine (Spindll): https://github.com/Iito/spindll
- GGUF via llama.cpp, native MLX on Apple Silicon, CUDA and Vulkan on NVIDIA
- OpenAI and Ollama API compatible — set one env var and existing tools work
- Auto-discovery on LAN, TLS encryption between every node
- Smart routing: requests go to the node with the model in memory and shortest queue
- Fair scheduling: per-user request queuing prevents any single user from monopolizing the cluster
- Model aliases: parley:code, parley:fast, parley:best, parley:reason
- Built-in web UI for mesh status and chat
- Free tier: up to 3 nodes

## Use cases

- Engineering teams sharing a large coding model across laptops
- Privacy-sensitive R&D where data must stay on-network
- Mixed-hardware offices (Metal, CUDA, CPU) pooled into one cluster
- Air-gapped environments with peer-to-peer model transfer
- Cost control: inference on hardware you already own, no per-request pricing
